title: Triangles
weightage: High — the most tested shape in GRE Geometry; the special right triangles appear again and again
intro: Triangles are the single most important shape on the GRE. The angle-sum rule, the Pythagorean theorem and the two special right triangles do most of the heavy lifting across the whole Geometry section, and they resurface inside quadrilateral, circle and coordinate-geometry problems too. The GRE deliberately does not test trigonometry — instead it reuses the 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles so often that memorising their side ratios is worth more than any other geometry fact. Two habits pay off constantly: recognise the common Pythagorean triples on sight, and remember that GRE figures are not drawn to scale, so a triangle that looks equilateral or right-angled is only so if the problem says so.

items.name: Exterior angle
items.formula: = sum of the two remote interior angles

topics.name: Angle Sum & Exterior Angle
topics.details: The three interior angles of any triangle add to 180° — the one fact you will use in nearly every triangle question. From it comes the exterior angle theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles it is not next to (the two "remote" interior angles). That shortcut saves a step whenever an angle sticks out beyond a side. When angles are given as a ratio, split 180° across the total number of parts. Because GRE figures are not drawn to scale, always assign the angles from the equations and never assume, from the look of the picture, that a triangle is equilateral or right-angled.

solved.problem: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 65°. Find the third.
An exterior angle of a triangle is 120°, and one remote interior angle is 45°. Find the other remote interior angle.
solved.solution: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 120 = 45 + x → x = 75°.

solved.problem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find each angle.
solved.solution: Total parts = 9, and 180° / 9 = 20° per part. Angles = 40°, 60°, 80°.

solved.problem: Quantitative Comparison. A triangle has angles x°, x°, and (x + 30)°. Quantity A: x. Quantity B: 50. Which is greater?
solved.solution: Sum: x + x + (x + 30) = 180 → 3x + 30 = 180 → 3x = 150 → x = 50. Quantity A = 50 = Quantity B, so the two are equal.

unsolved.problem: Two angles of a triangle are 37° and 53°. Find the third and classify the triangle.
An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and the two remote interior angles are equal. Find each remote interior angle.
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find the largest angle.
One angle of a triangle is 90°. A second angle is twice the third. Find the two remaining angles.
An exterior angle of a triangle measures 130° and one remote interior angle is 80°. Find the other remote interior angle.

topics.name: Types of Triangles
topics.details: Triangles are named two ways. By sides: scalene (all different), isosceles (two equal sides, and the angles opposite them are equal), and equilateral (all sides equal, every angle 60°). By angles: acute (all under 90°), right (one 90°), and obtuse (one over 90°). One rule quietly generates many GRE questions — the triangle inequality: any side must be less than the sum of the other two and greater than their difference. That constraint is exactly how the GRE asks "which of these could be the third side" or fixes an ambiguous isosceles triangle, since the picture is not to scale and cannot be measured.

solved.problem: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40°. Find each base angle.
solved.solution: The two base angles are equal and share the remaining 180 − 40 = 140°, so each = 140 / 2 = 70°.

solved.problem: One base angle of an isosceles triangle is 55°. Find the vertex angle.
solved.solution: Both base angles are 55°, so the vertex = 180 − (55 + 55) = 180 − 110 = 70°.

solved.problem: Two sides of a triangle are 5 and 9. Between what two values must the third side lie?
solved.solution: Triangle inequality: third side > 9 − 5 = 4 and < 9 + 5 = 14. So 4 < third side < 14.

solved.problem: An isosceles triangle has sides measuring 4 and 9 (each side is one of these two lengths). Find its perimeter.
solved.solution: The third side equals 4 or 9. A 4-4-9 triangle fails the inequality (4 + 4 = 8 < 9), so it must be 9-9-4. Perimeter = 9 + 9 + 4 = 22.

unsolved.problem: Find each interior angle of an equilateral triangle.
An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 100°. Find each base angle.
Two sides of a triangle are 6 and 10. Give the range of possible values for the third side.
An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 5 and a perimeter of 18. Find the base.
Can a triangle have side lengths 2, 3 and 6?

topics.name: The Pythagorean Theorem
topics.details: In any right triangle the square of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) equals the sum of the squares of the two legs: a² + b² = c². The GRE recycles a small set of whole-number right triangles — the Pythagorean triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 7-24-25, plus their multiples (6-8-10, 9-12-15, 10-24-26, and so on). Spotting a triple on sight saves you from squaring and taking a root on the slow on-screen calculator. When no triple appears, apply the formula directly and leave irrational answers in exact radical form unless a decimal is requested. Always confirm which side is the hypotenuse: it is opposite the right angle and is the longest side.

solved.problem: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Find the hypotenuse.
solved.solution: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, so the hypotenuse = √100 = 10 (a 3-4-5 triple doubled).

solved.problem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 and one leg of 5. Find the other leg.
A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. Find the hypotenuse.
solved.solution: This is 3-4-5 scaled by 3: 9 = 3×3, 12 = 3×4, so the hypotenuse = 3×5 = 15. (Check: 81 + 144 = 225 = 15².)

solved.problem: A rectangle measures 5 by 12. Find the length of its diagonal.
solved.solution: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and 12: √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.

unsolved.problem: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Find the hypotenuse.
A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 and a leg of 8. Find the other leg.
A right triangle has legs 8 and 15. Find the hypotenuse.
A right triangle has two legs each of length 6. Find the hypotenuse in exact form.
A 25-foot ladder rests against a wall with its base 7 feet from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?

topics.name: Special Right Triangles (45-45-90, 30-60-90)
topics.details: Because the GRE avoids trigonometry, it leans hard on two fixed-ratio right triangles, and memorising them is one of the highest-value moves in all of GRE prep. The 45-45-90 triangle (an isosceles right triangle, and half of a square along its diagonal) has sides in the ratio 1 : 1 : √2 — each leg times √2 gives the hypotenuse. The 30-60-90 triangle (half of an equilateral triangle) has sides in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2, where 1 is opposite the 30°, √3 is opposite the 60°, and 2 (the longest) is opposite the 90°. Anchor every 30-60-90 problem to the short leg (opposite 30°): double it for the hypotenuse, multiply it by √3 for the long leg. These show up whenever a square, an equilateral triangle, or a "nice" right triangle appears.

solved.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs of 5. Find the hypotenuse.
solved.solution: Hypotenuse = leg × √2 = 5√2.

solved.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of 10. Find each leg.
A 30-60-90 triangle has a short leg (opposite the 30° angle) of 4. Find the hypotenuse and the long leg.
solved.solution: Sides are in ratio 1 : √3 : 2 from the short leg. Hypotenuse = 2 × 4 = 8; long leg = 4√3.

solved.problem: A square has a diagonal of 8. Find the length of each side.
solved.solution: The diagonal splits the square into two 45-45-90 triangles with the diagonal as hypotenuse: side = 8 / √2 = (8√2) / 2 = 4√2.

unsolved.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs of 7. Find the hypotenuse.
A 30-60-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of 12. Find the short leg.
An equilateral triangle has a side of 6. Find its height.
hints: Short leg = 3, height is the long leg.

unsolved.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of 6√2. Find each leg.
A 30-60-90 triangle has a long leg (opposite the 60° angle) of 5√3. Find the short leg.

topics.name: Similar & Congruent Triangles
topics.details: Congruent triangles are identical — same angles and same side lengths (established by SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, or HL for right triangles). Similar triangles have the same shape but not necessarily the same size: their angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in a constant ratio. On the GRE, similarity is usually spotted by AA — if two angles match, the triangles are similar. Once similar, set up a proportion of corresponding sides to find a missing length. Two facts the GRE loves to test: the ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of sides, but the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of sides. Shadow and "distance across a river" problems are similar-triangle problems in disguise.

solved.problem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 3 : 5. A side of the smaller is 6. Find the corresponding side of the larger.
solved.solution: Set up the proportion 3/5 = 6/x → 3x = 30 → x = 10.

solved.problem: Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 2 : 3. The perimeter of the smaller is 24. Find the perimeter of the larger.
solved.solution: Perimeters share the side ratio: 2/3 = 24/P → 2P = 72 → P = 36.

solved.problem: Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 2 : 3. The area of the smaller is 8. Find the area of the larger.
A 6-foot-tall person casts a 4-foot shadow at the same time a tree casts a 20-foot shadow. Find the height of the tree.
solved.solution: The person and tree form similar right triangles: 6/4 = h/20 → 4h = 120 → h = 30 feet.

unsolved.problem: Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 1 : 4. A side of the smaller is 5. Find the corresponding side of the larger.
Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 3 : 4. The larger has a perimeter of 48. Find the smaller perimeter.
The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 9 : 16. Find the ratio of their corresponding sides.
hints: Side ratio is the square root of the area ratio.

unsolved.problem: A 5-foot pole casts a 3-foot shadow while a building casts a 24-foot shadow. Find the height of the building.
Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 2 : 5. The smaller has an area of 12. Find the area of the larger.

topics.name: Area of a Triangle
topics.details: The area of any triangle is ½ × base × height, where the height is the perpendicular distance from the chosen base to the opposite vertex — not a slanted side. In a right triangle the two legs are perpendicular, so they serve directly as base and height and the area is simply ½ × leg × leg. For an equilateral triangle of side s, the height is (s√3)/2, which gives the tidy formula Area = (√3/4) × s². A frequent GRE twist runs the formula backward: given the area and one dimension, solve for the other. Watch the on-screen basic calculator here — halving and multiplying are quick by hand, so reserve the calculator for the genuinely awkward numbers.

solved.problem: A triangle has a base of 10 and a height of 6. Find its area.
solved.solution: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30.

solved.problem: A right triangle has legs of 5 and 12. Find its area.
solved.solution: The legs are perpendicular, so Area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30.

solved.problem: Find the area of an equilateral triangle with a side of 4.
A triangle has an area of 20 and a base of 8. Find its height.
solved.solution: Area = ½ × base × height → 20 = ½ × 8 × h → 20 = 4h → h = 5.

unsolved.problem: A triangle has a base of 14 and a height of 5. Find its area.
A right triangle has legs of 6 and 8. Find its area.
hints: The legs are the base and height.

unsolved.problem: Find the area of an equilateral triangle with a side of 6.
A triangle has an area of 54 and a base of 12. Find its height.
A triangle has an area of 30 and a height of 5. Find its base.

shortcuts: Memorise the two special right triangles cold: 45-45-90 is 1 : 1 : √2, and 30-60-90 is 1 : √3 : 2 (short : long : hypotenuse). They replace all the trig the GRE deliberately leaves out.
Learn the Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25) and their multiples so you can read the third side without squaring anything.
Anchor every 30-60-90 to the short leg: hypotenuse = 2 × short, long leg = short × √3.
The height of an equilateral triangle of side s is (s√3)/2 — it is just the long leg of a 30-60-90.
Ratio of areas of similar triangles is the SQUARE of the side ratio; ratio of perimeters is the plain side ratio.
Shadow, ramp and "reflection" word problems are almost always similar-triangle proportions — set up matching sides over matching sides.
mistakes: Using a slanted side as the "height" in the area formula. The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base.
Assuming a triangle is right-angled, isosceles or equilateral because it looks that way. GRE figures are not drawn to scale.
Squaring the side ratio to get perimeters (it stays linear) or forgetting to square it for areas (it must be squared).
Mixing up the 30-60-90 sides — putting √3 opposite the 30° instead of the 60°. The short leg (×1) is always opposite the 30°.
Forgetting the triangle inequality when choosing a third side, so an "impossible" triangle slips through.
Calling the hypotenuse a leg. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is the longest side.

pyq.q: Quantitative Comparison — a right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Quantity A: the length of the hypotenuse. Quantity B: 10. Which is greater?
pyq.a: Equal. 6² + 8² = 100, so the hypotenuse is exactly 10 (the 3-4-5 triple doubled).

pyq.q: A GRE figure shows a triangle that looks equilateral but only marks two 60° angles. Is the third side equal to the others?
pyq.a: Two 60° angles force the third to be 60°, so it truly is equilateral — but you conclude that from the angle sum, not from the drawing, which is not to scale.

pyq.q: Numeric Entry — an equilateral triangle has a side of 10. Enter its height in the form a√3.
Two triangles are similar with side ratio 1 : 3. How many times larger is the bigger triangle’s area?
pyq.a: Area scales with the square of the side ratio: 3² = 9 times larger.

Third side lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two
a² + b² = c² (c is the hypotenuse)

summary: Triangles reward memory more than any other GRE topic. Lock in that the angles sum to 180°, that the Pythagorean theorem plus a handful of triples handle right triangles, and above all that the 45-45-90 (1 : 1 : √2) and 30-60-90 (1 : √3 : 2) ratios replace the trigonometry the GRE never asks for. Add the triangle inequality, the ½ × base × height area rule, and the similar-triangle proportions (with areas scaling as the square of the side ratio), and you can solve the great majority of GRE geometry. Trust the stated measurements, not the drawing — the figures are never guaranteed to be to scale.
